about.title: Personal Injury Help in Coalinga, California
about.longDescription: Coalinga sits along Rt 33, with Forest Avenue, E Polk Street, and E Elm Avenue carrying much of the town's daily traffic. In the most recent full year on record, Coalinga saw 11 injury collisions and 15 people hurt, with no traffic deaths reported. Those numbers reflect a small city, but any one of those collisions can turn a normal week into a stack of medical bills, missed work, and confusing paperwork. We handle personal injury claims in Coalinga and throughout Fresno County. Our team listens to what happened, evaluates your situation, and explains your options. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover money for you. If you were injured on Coalinga's roads, at work, or somewhere else in Fresno County, reaching out costs nothing and there's no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity was involved. Waiting too long can close the door on a claim entirely.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't End Your Case
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages, like pain and suffering, in typical personal injury cases. That means your claim isn't artificially capped before you even start.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we win or settle your case. That structure lets you get legal help without adding financial pressure to an already hard time.

items.question: Are you a law firm?
items.answer: We handle personal injury claims in Coalinga and Fresno County. We provide legal advice and represent you directly in your case.

items.question: How much does it cost to get your help?
items.answer: Nothing. Contacting us is free, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if we recover money for you. There's no upfront cost or obligation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have two years from the date of the injury to file a personal injury claim in California. If a government agency is involved, that window can be as short as six months, so it's worth acting sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Coalinga?
items.answer: Public collision records show that Rt 33, Forest Avenue, E Polk Street, and E Elm Avenue are among the higher-volume corridors for reported injury crashes in Coalinga. Reports also tend to cluster on Thursdays between roughly 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply record counts, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, so being partly at fault doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your final recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault, which we can help sort out.
